title: Classic Chicken Curry
description: A fragrant, rich chicken curry with tender pieces of chicken simmered in a golden coconut-tomato sauce. Warmly spiced with cumin, coriander, and turmeric — perfect for a cozy weeknight dinner.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Prepare the aromatics
1. Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
2. Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
GroupName : Build the sauce
3. Stir in curry powder, cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Toast spices for 30 seconds.
4. Add diced tomatoes and coconut milk. Stir to combine.
5. Season with salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
GroupName : Cook the chicken
6. Add cubed chicken breast. Stir to coat in the sauce.
7. Simmer for 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened.
8. Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve over basmati rice.
equipment:
Large skillet or dutch oven
Wooden spoon
Sharp knife
Cutting board
notes:
For a richer curry, use chicken thighs instead of breast.
Add a handful of spinach at the end for extra nutrition.
Leftovers taste even better the next day as the flavours deepen.

title: Blueberry Muffins
description: Soft, bakery-style blueberry muffins with a golden dome and bursting fresh blueberries in every bite. A classic breakfast treat that takes less than 30 minutes start to finish.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, melted butter, milk, and vanilla extract.
4. Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently until just combined — do not overmix.
5. Fold in the blueberries carefully.
6. Divide batter evenly among the 12 muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full.
7. Bake for 18-20 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean and tops are golden.
8. Cool in tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
equipment:
12-cup muffin tin
Muffin liners
Mixing bowls
Whisk
Rubber spatula
notes:
Do not overmix the batter — lumps are fine and lead to a more tender muffin.
Fresh or frozen blueberries both work. If using frozen, do not thaw first.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

title: Classic Bolognese
description: A slow-cooked Italian meat sauce that clings beautifully to tagliatelle or pappardelle. Made with a soffritto base, ground beef, pancetta, white wine, and a splash of milk for silky richness.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Soffritto base
1. Heat olive oil and butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
2. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly golden.
GroupName : Brown the meat
3. Add pancetta and cook for 3 minutes until it renders its fat.
4. Add ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon. Season with salt and pepper. Cook until no pink remains, about 8 minutes.
GroupName : Build the sauce
5. Pour in white wine and cook until evaporated, about 3 minutes.
6. Add whole milk, stir, and cook until absorbed, about 5 minutes.
7. Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
8. Add canned crushed tomatoes. Stir to combine. Reduce heat to very low.
9. Simmer uncovered for 1.5-2 hours, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thick and rich.
10. Taste, adjust seasoning. Serve over fresh tagliatelle with grated Parmigiano.
equipment:
Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven
Wooden spoon
Sharp knife
Cutting board
notes:
The longer the simmer, the better the bolognese. Don't rush it.
Freeze the sauce in portions for up to 3 months.
Authentic bolognese uses very little tomato — resist the urge to add more.

title: Classic Banana Bread
description: Moist, tender banana bread packed with ripe banana flavour and a hint of vanilla. Perfect for using up overripe bananas — this loaf disappears fast.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Grease a 9×5 inch loaf pan.
2. In a large bowl, mash the bananas with a fork until smooth.
3. Mix in melted butter, sugar, egg, and vanilla extract.
4. Sprinkle baking soda and salt over the mixture and stir to combine.
5. Fold in flour until just combined. Do not overmix.
6. Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan.
7. Bake for 55-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
8. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
equipment:
9x5 inch loaf pan
Large mixing bowl
Fork or potato masher
Rubber spatula
notes:
The riper and blacker the bananas, the sweeter and more flavourful the bread.
Add chocolate chips or walnuts for extra texture.
Wrap in cling film and store at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze sliced.

title: Hearty Beef Stew
description: A soul-warming beef stew with melt-in-your-mouth chunks of braised beef, tender vegetables, and a deep, glossy wine-enriched broth. Perfect for cold evenings and meal prep.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Prep and sear
1. Pat beef dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
2. Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides, 3-4 minutes per batch. Set aside.
3. Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes.
4. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 1 minute.
GroupName : Build the stew
5. Pour in red wine, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom.
6. Add beef broth, thyme, bay leaves, and Worcestershire sauce. Return beef to pot.
7. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours.
GroupName : Add vegetables
8. Add potatoes and carrots. Cook uncovered for 30 more minutes until vegetables are tender.
9. Mix cornstarch with cold water, stir into stew to thicken.
10. Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Serve in bowls.
equipment:
Large Dutch oven
Wooden spoon
Sharp knife
Cutting board
notes:
Use a well-marbled cut like chuck roast for the best texture — it becomes incredibly tender.
Make it a day ahead; it tastes even better reheated.
Store in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze for 3 months.

title: Homemade Granola
description: Crunchy, clusters of golden oats tossed with honey, coconut oil, almonds, and seeds. Incredibly versatile — serve with yoghurt, milk, or straight out of the jar.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, mix together oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, cinnamon, and salt.
3. In a small saucepan, warm honey and coconut oil over low heat until melted. Add vanilla extract.
4. Pour the liquid over the oat mixture. Stir until everything is well coated.
5. Spread evenly on the baking sheet in a thin layer.
6. Bake for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden brown.
7. Remove from oven. Do not stir while cooling — this creates the clusters.
8. Cool completely on the pan. Stir in dried cranberries. Store in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks.
equipment:
Large baking sheet
Parchment paper
Large mixing bowl
Small saucepan
notes:
Do not stir the granola while it cools — this is what creates the beloved clusters.
Customise with any nuts, seeds, or dried fruits you like.
For extra-chunky granola, press down firmly with a spatula before baking.

title: Crispy Falafel
description: Light, herby, and irresistibly crispy falafel made from scratch with soaked chickpeas, fresh herbs, and aromatic spices. Serve in pita with tahini and pickled vegetables.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Make the falafel mixture
1. Drain soaked chickpeas (do NOT use canned — they must be dried soaked chickpeas).
2. Place chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander, and salt in a food processor.
3. Pulse until finely ground but not a paste — the mixture should hold together when pressed.
4. Transfer to a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
GroupName : Shape and cook
5. Add baking powder and flour to the mixture. Stir to combine.
6. Using wet hands, shape 2 tablespoons of mixture into small patties or balls.
7. Heat 5cm of oil in a deep skillet to 175°C (350°F).
8. Fry falafel in batches for 3-4 minutes until deep golden on all sides.
9. Drain on paper towels. Serve immediately with tahini sauce, pita, and fresh salad.
equipment:
Food processor
Deep skillet or pot
Thermometer
Slotted spoon
Paper towels
notes:
You must use dried chickpeas soaked overnight, not canned — canned chickpeas are too wet.
The mixture can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours before frying.
For baked falafel: brush with oil and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes, flipping halfway.

title: Classic French Crêpes
description: Delicate, paper-thin crêpes with lightly crisp edges and a buttery flavour. Fill them sweet with lemon and sugar, or savoury with ham and cheese — endlessly versatile.
author: Meal Prep Codex
instructions:
GroupName : Make the batter
1. In a blender, combine flour, eggs, milk, water, melted butter, sugar, vanilla extract, and salt.
2. Blend on high for 30 seconds until completely smooth.
3. Rest batter in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes (or overnight). This relaxes the gluten.
GroupName : Cook the crêpes
4. Heat a 20-22cm non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Lightly brush with butter.
5. Pour 3-4 tablespoons of batter into the pan, immediately swirling to coat the pan in a thin layer.
6. Cook for 60-90 seconds until the edges start to lift and the surface looks set.
7. Flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds until lightly golden.
8. Slide onto a plate. Repeat with remaining batter, stacking crêpes between parchment paper.
9. Serve with lemon juice and icing sugar, or your favourite fillings.
equipment:
Blender or mixing bowl
20-22cm non-stick crêpe pan
Heat-resistant pastry brush
Spatula
notes:
Resting the batter is key — don't skip it.
The first crêpe is always a test crêpe — adjust heat and batter amount as needed.
Crepe batter keeps in the fridge for 2 days.
